Tatjana Belmar.kurzprofil: For many years I have been committed, with heart and conviction as well as great attentiveness and in-depth expertise, to victim support in the field of social compensation law (Soziales Entschädigungsrecht) and the related assistance and care benefits.
Tatjana Belmar.profil:
For many years I have been committed, with heart and conviction as well as great attentiveness and in-depth expertise, to victim support in the field of social compensation law (Soziales Entschädigungsrecht) and the related assistance and care benefits.

My path into this work has been shaped by personal experiences in my childhood and by the wish to offer other people guidance, understanding and support.

Since 2016 I have been an administrator of the Facebook group “Opferentschädigungsgesetz/Soziales Entschädigungsrecht” (Crime Victims Compensation Act/Social Compensation Law). Since 2019 I have also been the founder and administrator of the group “Austausch zum Fonds sexueller Missbrauch” (Exchange on the Fund for Sexual Abuse).

I also bring various professional qualifications with me. I trained as an IT systems management assistant (IT-Systemkauffrau) and as an integrative psychotherapist under the Non-Medical Practitioners Act (Heilpraktikergesetz, HPG), specialising in trauma following harmful events (schädigende Ereignisse) and violent crimes. In addition, I have gained a master’s qualification in hypnosis with a focus on trauma, and I am a trained multiplier for addiction prevention as well as a mediator. Beyond that, I spent two years taking part in a DBT group project (dialectical behaviour therapy) for people with borderline diagnoses and co-founded the Borderline Trialogue in Lübeck and Hamburg.

Something I care about deeply is treating people’s vulnerability with care when they come into contact with bureaucratic structures. Application procedures should support people – not burden them further or retraumatise them. That is what I stand up for, with clarity and with empathy.

It was only decades later that I was able to name the harmful events and violent crimes I experienced, and only around 33 years after the crimes – accompanied by a lack of knowledge and by deep feelings of guilt and shame – was I able to submit an application for benefits under the Crime Victims Compensation Act. Since 2013 I have been in an application process that is still ongoing today. Among other things, it has been marked by doubts about my credibility, missing witnesses and records whose retention periods have expired. These many years of dispute have left many marks and have brought with them a lasting toll on my physical and mental health. Through my visibility I want to give others courage, because through intensive exchange with other people affected I became increasingly aware: I am not alone in this. I am KE!N EINZELFALL.

From this realisation grew the wish to change something – to create more visibility, to open up spaces for exchange and to give those affected a voice, but at the same time also to provide information for relatives and professionals directly from those affected, in order to clear up prejudices and misunderstandings.

This concern was a key reason for co-founding the association KE!N EINZELFALL e. V. With my professional training, my personal story and my values, I stand by the association as well as those affected, relatives, anyone interested and professionals – with empathy, reflection and commitment, and above all with respect and on an equal footing.

Franziska Künstler.kurzprofil: My motivation for getting involved in victim support stems from being affected myself and from the fact that I – like many others – only found out about social compensation law by chance.
Franziska Künstler.profil:
Affected in various contexts outside the family

Dual study programme at the Federal University of Applied Administrative Sciences (Fachhochschule des Bundes für öffentliche Verwaltung) in Berlin, Department of Social Insurance – specialising in pension law

Involved in Sachsen-Anhalt in a nationwide petition for improvements to social compensation law (soziales Entschädigungsrecht), initiated by Gudrun Stifter

My motivation for getting involved in victim support stems from being affected myself and from the fact that I – like many others – only found out about social compensation law by chance.

Having the consequences of a harmful event (schädigendes Ereignis) recognised under social law, whether as a degree of disability (Grad der Behinderung, GdB) or as a degree of damage-related impairment (Grad der Schädigungsfolgen, GdS), is sadly not a given, but usually a long struggle. And that struggle does not end with recognition either; it leads to further disputes over benefits to which one is clearly entitled, but which are then hardly ever granted.

At some point my school-leaving motto, “Live and let live”, was no longer enough for me, and when someone asks me today why I stand up against injustice in our association, the answer is simple:

It is not about whether I am entitled to benefits; it is about the principle. I do not want to rest on my own status, but to help others obtain what they are entitled to as well.

Within the limits of what my own life story and my trauma-related disorders allow, I campaign for improvements in the application process, and for visibility and understanding from the perspective of those affected.

However individual each case may be, neither the Crime Victims Compensation Act (Opferentschädigungsgesetz, OEG) nor Book XIV of the Social Code (Sozialgesetzbuch XIV, SGB XIV) is a niche law that is hardly ever applied. The annual statistics of the Weisser Ring show that hurdles in the application process lead to rejections in many cases.

These are not isolated cases – regrettably, there is often a system behind them.

Petra Hildebrandt.profil:
As the relative of a woman who has been affected, supporting people who have experienced violence is very close to my heart. That is why I want to bring my many years of professional experience as an industrial clerk (Industriekauffrau) to the work of KE!N EINZELFALL e.V.

Since its founding, I have supported KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. as treasurer through reliable and transparent financial management. My aim is to ensure that all funds are used responsibly, so as to further the association’s work and the support it provides in the best possible way.

I am glad to be part of this committed team as treasurer and to be able to make a small but important contribution through my work. Together with the team, I want to make sure that every donation and every euro is used responsibly where it is needed – for more help, visibility and information.

Nicole Khalil.kurzprofil: I am a Berliner, a single mother of two children, and I know life from different perspectives that are often at play at the same time.
Nicole Khalil.profil:
I am a Berliner, a single mother of two children, and I know life from different perspectives that are often at play at the same time.

My view of victim support, inclusion and social support has been shaped by my own experiences, by many years of responsibility for others and by a deep wish to give people guidance, understanding and relief.

For many years I have been involved, with heart, conviction and great sensitivity, at the point where being affected oneself, the perspective of relatives and responsibility towards society meet.

I am affected myself, but at the same time I am also the relative of a mentally ill mother whose illness is the result of what she herself was affected by. Over many years I experienced first-hand the challenges this brings in terms of care, looking after someone, responsibility and being overwhelmed.

It was only much later that I began to engage intensively with my own experience of being affected. Quite apart from that, I have been living with epilepsy for many years. As a result, I have extensive experience of the law on severe disability (Schwerbehindertenrecht) and of inclusion – particularly in the areas of work, school and social life. I know what it feels like when structures that are meant to support you do not always do so, and how much strength it takes to find your way through systems that rarely reflect the whole reality of a person’s life.

It is precisely the many layers of my life story that have sharpened my perspective. I know what it is like to carry responsibility while needing support yourself.

These experiences feed into my involvement – with respect for each person’s life story and without hasty judgements. Something I care about deeply is treating people with sensitivity when they are confronted with authorities, benefit systems and formal procedures.

Bureaucratic processes must not cause additional hurt or strain. They should offer stability, not reinforce powerlessness. That is what I stand up for – clearly, taking the side of those affected, and with an approach that puts the person at the centre.

I am a founding member of KE!N EINZELFALL e. V. and act as substitute for the Chair. In Berlin I also work for the association as its representative on the State Advisory Council for People with Disabilities (Landesbeiratsbeauftragte für Menschen mit Behinderung). In this role I contribute my experience, my range of perspectives and my network in order to give those affected, relatives and professionals a hearing and to help shape lasting change.

My commitment is driven by the conviction that no one is alone with their story. That being affected has many faces. And that visibility, exchange and mutual recognition are crucial steps on the way to more justice, inclusion and humanity. With my values, my life skills and my lived experience, I stand by those affected, relatives, those indirectly affected, anyone interested and professionals – with respect, commitment and on an equal footing. Because one thing matters to me: We are KE!N EINZELFALL

Tanja Häfner.kurzprofil: For over 17 years I worked in criminal defence and experienced the system from a perspective directly opposed to that of those affected. I saw how proceedings are conducted, how people speak, what dynamics ari...
Tanja Häfner.profil:
For over 17 years I worked in criminal defence and experienced the system from a perspective directly opposed to that of those affected. I saw how proceedings are conducted, how people speak, what dynamics arise – and at some point it became ever clearer to me how great the distance between the system and those affected really is.

There came a point when I realised: I do not want this any more. I no longer wanted to use my knowledge on that side, but to make a deliberate change of perspective – towards the people who need support, guidance and protection. For more than 12 years now I have been working in the public sector, and so I now also know this side of the structures, the processes and the limits. It is precisely these experiences that show me how important it is to create spaces that work differently: accessible, understandable and trauma-sensitive.

Today it matters to me to pass on all my knowledge and make it useful for those affected. I want to help them find their way around the system better, understand what is happening – and no longer feel at its mercy.

At KE!N EINZELFALL e. V. I serve as Data Protection Officer. For me, data protection means far more than legal requirements – it is the foundation of trust. People who come to us must be able to rely on their information being protected, on their story staying where they want it to stay, and on being able to decide for themselves how visible they want to be. That is why I work to ensure that our platform is a protected space – technically, structurally and on a human level. A space in which anonymity is possible, in which there need be no fear of judgement or consequences, and in which people can open up when they are ready.

I have got to know both sides of the system – and I have made a conscious decision to stand on the side of those affected. I want to break down barriers, create safety and shape spaces that make it clear: Together: KE!N EINZELFALL!

André Bauer.kurzprofil: I volunteer with KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. because I want to help ensure that those affected, those indirectly affected and relatives are heard more and find more support. Many experiences remain hidden for a long time or are only noticed wh...
André Bauer.profil:
I volunteer with KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. because I want to help ensure that those affected, those indirectly affected and relatives are heard more and find more support. Many experiences remain hidden for a long time or are only noticed when someone tells them, puts them into context and passes them on.

In the association’s social media work I see the opportunity to create spaces for exactly that. Posts can make the voices of those affected visible, share knowledge, give practical tips, point to opportunities for exchange and put important developments into context. In this way, social media can be more than just public relations: it can give people guidance, ease their burden and show them that they are not alone with their experiences.

In my job I deal a great deal with communication, text, images and digital media. I bring this background to the association’s social media work in order to prepare content clearly, respectfully and carefully — always with the aim of putting the issues and voices of those affected more firmly at the centre.

I am glad to be part of this committed team and to be able to make a small but important contribution through my work — for more awareness, guidance and compassion. So that one day no one has to say any more: “I didn’t know.”

Herr und Frau Unbekannt.untertitel: This portrait stands for the people who support KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. but whose identities must remain protected for safety reasons.
Herr und Frau Unbekannt.kurzprofil: The voices of courage, in the background and hidden, because there are people who work every day for KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. – and yet have to remain invisible. Not out of reticence. Not out of distance. But because their reality allows nothing else. They l...
Herr und Frau Unbekannt.profil: The voices of courage, in the background and hidden, because there are people who work every day for KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. – and yet have to remain invisible. Not out of reticence. Not out of distance. But because their reality allows nothing else. They live with protective measures that shape their lives: with blocks on the disclosure of their address from the population register (Auskunftssperren), with security restrictions, with the fear of being found, with the quiet but ever-present need to protect themselves and their loved ones. Many of them have experienced violence, have testified, have resisted – and still bear the consequences today. For them, being visible is not a right. It is a risk. And yet they choose to be there. To help. To fight. Quietly and without applause. Their visibility lies in the hidden – and is an indispensable part, of immeasurable importance, of what we make visible. Their commitment is not a public statement – it is a daily decision against fear and for others who are affected. Every act of support, every action takes strength and an inner greatness that can never be honoured enough. Every contribution, every decision these people make is carried by courage. By a courage that is not loud – but deep. Quiet. Unshakeable. They have our deepest respect. Our most sincere thanks. For their courage. For their perseverance. For everything they carry without being seen. That their names do not appear here is not an absence. It is protection. A necessary one. One to be taken seriously. And perhaps also the most striking proof of how much is at stake. And perhaps that is the greatest truth of all: that the strongest forces are often the ones you cannot see; even so, we will not give up on giving the hidden, unreported cases (Dunkelfeld) the chance to become more visible – step by step, voice by voice. For more visibility, for being heard and for support.

Nils-Digital.untertitel: Development and technical support for this website
Nils-Digital.kurzprofil: We are Nils-Digital and we built the new website for KE!N EINZELFALL e.V.
Nils-Digital.profil:
We are Nils-Digital and we built the new website for KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. We continue to look after the technology behind it.

A website for people who have been affected has to do more than look good. Anyone reading it should feel safe. It is just as important to us that everyone can use the site, which is why we have placed great emphasis on accessibility.

Behind Nils-Digital are Nils Nehring and Kevin Herrmann. We develop websites, apps and AI automations for businesses, the self-employed and associations. We look after every project personally, with short lines of communication and clear agreements.

We are delighted to be accompanying the association on this journey. Because the more easily people who have been affected can find what they are looking for here, the sooner they realise: they are not an isolated case.
